I have read the relevant legislation and guidelines in GERMANY for biosafety requirements etc. and it is genuinely somewhat ambiguous as to which biosafety level blood samples actually need to be processed under.

The clearest, and interestingly the ONLY unambiguous statement I have found so far, is in this guidance document from @unigoettingen@academiccloud.social #UMG:

See image.

uncertainty because blood is classified as S3 when screening tests for HIV, HBV or HCV are positive. If the work is targeted at S3 pathogens, it must be carried out under S3 conditions. However, non-targeted activities may also be performed under S2 conditions, even if the sample contains an S3 pathogen.

But what about a sample that has been screened and tested negative for HIV, HBV, HCV, etc.? If the sample is then considered S2, but the activity is not targeted at an S2 pathogen, can it actually be processed under S1 conditions?

Or does this also depend on whether the sample comes from an asymptomatic patient?

Would a patient who simply feels unwell already be considered symptomatic in this context?

required screening of every sample beforehand, which is practically impossible if samples come from external laboratories or patients for follow-up testing.

Is it sufficient to open and pipette S2 samples in an S1 laboratory,inside a S2 safety cabinet?
